summary: An AutoDeal Philippines feature article by Earl Lee, dated Aug 24, 2023, warns drivers about road hazards that appear or emerge after heavy rain. It covers potholes, uneven road surfaces and waves, trash and debris, fallen trees and landslides, and road repair works, advising drivers to slow down and heed signs. The rest of the page is site navigation and unrelated promotional content.
one_line: AutoDeal Philippines article warning drivers about potholes, debris, fallen trees, landslides and roadworks that follow heavy rain.
key_facts: The article 'After the rain: Road hazards to watch out for' was written by Earl Lee and dated Aug 24, 2023 on AutoDeal's car features section.
Rainwater can wash away the top layer of asphalt, and major road damage can expose the concrete base, creating a dip and a potentially sharp lip.
Potholes can wreak havoc on a car's rims and perhaps even its suspension, even at reasonable speeds.
Uneven waves and divots in the road can influence steering or even cause a driver to lose control.
On off-camber road surfaces with no space to maneuver, the article advises drivers to grip the steering wheel properly and be prepared to catch it.
Trash and debris such as plastic bottles, loose asphalt and rocks can be carried onto the road, especially when it floods, reducing traction.
A tire that rolls over anything other than asphalt or concrete may lose some traction.
Fallen trees can bring traffic to a screeching halt until a clearing operation removes the obstruction.
Trees may fall even in the city, especially after a storm with strong winds.
Landslides are common on mountain roads and may block the entire thoroughfare or roadway depending on severity.
The article advises drivers to slow down at all times after a storm.
Local government units and other bodies are likely to contract workers to fix storm damage right after or a while after the calamity.
Road repair workers are required to properly indicate and block off the section of road they are working on.
The article's opening line is 'When it rains it pours, and while the rain itself is already a road hazard that keeps us in our homes'.
The article is tagged with rain, rainstorm, Typhoon, Hurricane and Road Safety.
